rationale: Edge-case lens ran clean and all 3 candidates verified as real, reachable defects in the restyled .top-banner card: the runUpdateApp() error path still appends .update-error as an unstyled flex sibling with no wrap rule, .top-banner-body has no flex-basis/min-width guard against long version strings, and data-busy is set on #update-banner but has no matching CSS so buttons disable functionally without looking disabled. No story/spec artifact exists for this ticket (acceptance lens not dispatched), so business_review is empty and confidence is capped low; standards review was intentionally skipped for the compact profile (no guide/audit applicable). 0 deferred, 0 dismissed.

findings.title: Update-app error text overlaps banner row
findings.problem: runUpdateApp()'s catch block appends .update-error directly as a 3rd flex child of #app-update-banner (a .top-banner). .top-banner has no flex-wrap and the .update-error rule (display:block; width:100%) only sets flex-basis inside the nowrap row — it does not push onto a new line.
findings.impact: When an app update fails, the error text is squeezed into or overlaps the title/line/actions row instead of wrapping below it, on the exact path most likely to be exercised (a failed update).
findings.recommendation: Append .update-error inside .top-banner-body (or give .top-banner flex-wrap: wrap and .update-error flex-basis: 100%) so the error line breaks onto its own row.

findings.title: Top-banner card has no wrap/min-width guard
findings.problem: .top-banner is a nowrap flex row; .top-banner-body has no flex-basis, flex-grow, or min-width:0, and .top-banner-actions is flex:none, so long CLI/app version strings or a narrow window have no defined shrink/wrap behavior for the title/line text.
findings.impact: Long version strings (e.g. long semver/build identifiers) or a narrowed app window can overflow or clip the banner title/line, or push the action buttons out of the row, undermining the card layout the ticket asks for.
findings.recommendation: Add flex-wrap: wrap to .top-banner and flex: 1 1 auto; min-width: 0 to .top-banner-body so text wraps within the card instead of overflowing.

findings.title: Busy update-banner buttons have no visual disabled state
findings.problem: setInstallRunning() sets #update-banner's dataset.busy and disables update-banner-run/-dismiss, but styles.css defines a busy rule only for #app-sidebar[data-busy="1"] — there is no #update-banner[data-busy="1"] (or .top-banner[data-busy]) rule, so the buttons carry no dimmed/disabled look while a run is in flight.
findings.impact: Directly misses the ticket's stated requirement that buttons "look disabled while the old wizard runs (data-busy)" — during an install the CLI-update banner's buttons are inert but visually indistinguishable from active ones.
findings.recommendation: Add a CSS rule such as #update-banner[data-busy="1"] .top-banner-action, #update-banner[data-busy="1"] .top-banner-dismiss { opacity: .5; } to match the sidebar's existing busy treatment.
